title: China-to-Slovakia EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: EU public AC recharging points are subject to AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804) requirements for connector availability. AFIR Annex II specifies Type 2 for normal-power AC recharging points. IEC/EN 62196-2 describes the Type 2 technical connector design; the legal obligation is AFIR, while the IEC/EN standard is the technical specification route. AFIR is directly applicable in Slovakia without transposition and has applied to new public charging pools from 13 April 2024.
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T 20234.2 for AC charging, which defines a physically distinct 7-pin connector incompatible with IEC Type 2. GB/T plugs cannot mate with EU Type 2 sockets.
rows.gap: Hardware connector is physically incompatible. A Chinese EV or EVSE designed only around a GB/T AC interface cannot interoperate with EU public Type 2 AC infrastructure in Slovakia without a physical inlet/socket and control-interface redesign. The connector body, pin count, and locking mechanism all differ. AFIR is directly applicable in Slovakia and any adapter strategy for public infrastructure must be checked against AFIR and Slovak safety rules rather than treated as a substitute for compliant connector design.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR requirements for publicly accessible AC recharging points in Slovakia, including Type 2 availability as specified in Annex II. IEC/EN 62196-2 is the voluntary technical connector standard/specification used to implement that legal requirement; it is not the legal obligation by itself.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic market — GB/T 20234.2 required for EV sold in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant for EU/Slovak public charging interoperability as-is if the product only supports GB/T AC. EU public AC infrastructure in Slovakia must meet AFIR connector requirements, and IEC/EN 62196-2 Type 2 is the technical specification used for that route. GB/T AC interfaces are not a substitute for AFIR-compliant Type 2 compatibility.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)

rows.target_requirement: EU public DC recharging points are subject to AFIR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1804) requirements for connector availability. AFIR Annex II specifies Combo 2 for high-power DC recharging points. IEC/EN 62196-3 describes the CCS Combo 2 technical connector design; the legal obligation is AFIR, while the IEC/EN standard is the technical specification route. AFIR is directly applicable in Slovakia without transposition.
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB/T 20234.3 for DC fast charging, defining a physically distinct 9-pin connector (CHAdeMO-influenced design) incompatible with CCS Combo 2. The pin layout, communication protocol (CAN vs. PLC), and inlet shape all differ.
rows.gap: Hardware connector is physically incompatible. Chinese EVs or EVSE with only a GB/T DC interface cannot fast-charge at Slovak/EU CCS2 public stations without hardware and communication-stack redesign. The vehicle/charger communication stack (GB/T 27930 CAN vs. ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 PLC pathways common in EU CCS practice) also differs, compounding the incompatibility beyond the physical plug. Any adapter strategy for public infrastructure must be checked against AFIR and Slovak safety rules.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR requirements for publicly accessible high-power DC recharging points in Slovakia, including Combo 2 availability as specified in Annex II. IEC/EN 62196-3 is the voluntary technical connector standard/specification used to implement that legal requirement; it is not the legal obligation by itself.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic market — GB/T 20234.3 required for DC fast-charge EV sold in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant for EU/Slovak public DC charging interoperability as-is if the product only supports GB/T DC. EU public DC infrastructure in Slovakia must meet AFIR connector requirements, and IEC/EN 62196-3 CCS Combo 2 is the technical specification used for that route. GB/T DC interfaces are not a substitute for AFIR-compliant Combo 2 compatibility.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)

rows.requirement: Legal Mandate: AFIR vs. AFID and Transition Timeline
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) replaced Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID) with binding targets. AFIR entered into force 13 April 2024. New public charging pools must comply from that date; all existing pools must be upgraded to Type 2 / CCS2 by 2025–2026 depending on power level. AFIR is directly applicable in all EU member states including Slovakia without transposition.
rows.china_equivalent: China's equivalent policy mandate is GB/T 20234 series (enforced via MIIT type-approval). No bilateral connector recognition or mutual acceptance agreement exists between China GB/T and EU IEC 62196 standards. (Confirmed: no bilateral connector or certification mutual recognition treaty between CN GB/T 20234 and EU IEC 62196 has been concluded as of June 2026.)
rows.gap: No harmonisation or mutual recognition between GB/T and IEC 62196 series. AFIR is a binding EU Regulation (not a Directive), meaning no member-state flexibility — Slovakia cannot accept GB/T connectors for public infrastructure. Any EV destined for the Slovak/EU market must carry Type 2 (AC) and CCS Combo 2 (DC) inlets as a hard market-entry requirement.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: AFIR is directly applicable across EU member states including Slovakia from 13 April 2024 for in-scope publicly accessible recharging infrastructure. IEC/EN 62196 connector standards are technical specifications referenced/used to implement AFIR connector requirements, not standalone legal obligations.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory domestically; no reciprocal obligation on EU side to accept GB/T

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Non-compliant as-is for Slovak/EU public charging infrastructure where a product relies on Chinese GB/T connectors only. AFIR creates the binding EU obligation for in-scope public infrastructure in Slovakia; Type 2 / Combo 2 technical compatibility is the practical redesign item. This is a product and infrastructure interoperability gap, not merely a documentation gap.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)

rows.requirement: DSO / SEPS Grid Connection — 230/400 V 50 Hz Slovak National Grid
rows.target_requirement: Slovakia's electricity supply system is operated at transmission level by SEPS (Slovenská elektrizačná prenosová sústava) and at distribution level by regional DSOs (Západoslovenská distribučná, Stredoslovenská distribučná, Východoslovenská distribučná), all under ÚRSO (Regulatory Office for Network Industries) sector oversight. The low-voltage context is 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz. That is the same frequency as China but a different nominal voltage from China's 220/380 V baseline. Grid-connected charger projects should be treated as site-specific electrical installations requiring DSO supply-capacity review, protection coordination, metering, earthing, harmonic and power-quality review, commissioning, and written project acceptance before energisation. EU Regulation (EU) 2016/631 (RfG) applies for installations above the Slovak thresholds.
target_standards: SEPS (Slovak Electricity Transmission System) grid-connection technical requirements — https://www.sepsas.sk
DSO (Západoslovenská distribučná / Stredoslovenská distribučná / Východoslovenská distribučná) connection requirements
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-1 — EV conductive charging system general requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic charger installations are commonly documented under GB/T 18487.1-2023, GB/T 20234 connector standards, GB/T 27930-2023 for DC communication, and local grid-operator acceptance. China domestic supply is 220 V single-phase / 380 V three-phase at 50 Hz. The shared 50 Hz frequency does not mean voltage equivalence: Slovakia 230/400 V requires input-voltage, protection-threshold, thermal, and metering validation beyond the China baseline.
china_standards: China local grid operator project-acceptance requirements
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm that the charger covers 230 V single-phase / 400 V three-phase at 50 Hz, not only China's 220/380 V settings. Protection thresholds, leakage-current devices, metering accuracy, harmonic emissions, supply-capacity calculations, earthing, surge protection, and commissioning documents should be prepared for DSO/SEPS review. Slovak or EU-official-language documentation is typically required for DSO connection applications and building permits. For large installations interfacing with the Slovak transmission grid, SEPS technical requirements apply in addition to the EU RfG Regulation.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — grid-connected installations require DSO/SEPS project review and acceptance under ÚRSO framework; voltage is 230/400 V at 50 Hz, which differs from China 220/380 V despite the same frequency
mandatory_status.cn: China grid-operator acceptance applies domestically and is not a Slovak DSO/SEPS approval substitute; China 220/380 V evidence must be revalidated for Slovakia 230/400 V

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Slovakia-ready EVSE needs DSO/SEPS project acceptance and explicit 230/400 V 50 Hz validation. Do not describe the voltage as matching China: only the 50 Hz frequency matches, while nominal voltage differs from China's 220/380 V baseline. Slovak or EU-official-language documentation is expected for permitting.

rows.requirement: CE Conformity Assessment — LVD, EMC, RED (if wireless)
rows.target_requirement: EV chargers sold in Slovakia (EU) must bear the CE marking, demonstrating conformity with all applicable EU legislation. Wired AC/DC chargers typically fall under LVD (2014/35/EU) and EMC Directive (2014/30/EU); chargers with wireless communication (e.g., Wi-Fi, Bluetooth for smart charging) additionally require conformity with RED (2014/53/EU). Conformity is generally established by manufacturer self-declaration supported by a technical file. Harmonised EN standards are voluntary routes to presumption of conformity, not mandatory legal requirements in themselves. ÚNMS SR is the Slovak market surveillance authority for CE-marked products.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-21-2 (EMC for off-board EV chargers)
rows.china_equivalent: In China, EV chargers require China Compulsory Certification (CCC) under the GB/T and GB standards regime. Key standards include GB/T 18487.1 (AC charging system) and GB/T 20234 series (connectors). CCC is a mandatory third-party certification through designated bodies (CABs); it does not involve self-declaration and is structurally different from CE's conformity-based model.
rows.gap: Chinese manufacturers must obtain CE marking via EU-recognised conformity assessment routes (self-declaration under harmonised EN standards or notified-body involvement for certain RED equipment). CCC certification is not recognised in Slovakia/EU and does not substitute for CE. Manufacturers must generate EU-specific technical documentation, test reports referencing EN standards, and an EU Declaration of Conformity — none of which are produced as part of the CCC process. Technical documentation should include Slovak or EU-official-language versions of user instructions and installation manuals.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: CE marking and conformity with all applicable EU directives/regulations before Slovak/EU market access. Harmonised EN standards are voluntary presumption-of-conformity tools; alternatives are allowed if compliance is demonstrated.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking is mandatory before placing EV chargers on the Slovak/EU market. CCC does not substitute for CE. Manufacturers must independently build EU technical files and, for wireless-enabled chargers, ensure RED compliance where applicable. ÚNMS SR is the Slovak market surveillance authority.

rows.requirement: EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC) and Technical File
rows.target_requirement: Before placing a product on the Slovak/EU market, the manufacturer (or its EU authorised representative) must draw up an EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC) listing all applicable directives and the harmonised standards applied, and must compile and retain a technical file for at least 10 years. The DoC must be made available to market surveillance authorities on request, including ÚNMS SR in Slovakia. Requirements are set out in each applicable directive (LVD Art. 15, EMCD Art. 14, RED Art. 19) and in Decision 768/2008/EC (modular conformity assessment).
rows.china_equivalent: Under the Chinese CCC regime, the equivalent documentary output is the CCC certificate issued by the designated certification body, accompanied by type-test reports. There is no manufacturer self-declaration equivalent to the EU DoC; the certificate is issued by a third party. Post-certificate, manufacturers must maintain a production consistency system audited periodically by the CAB.
china_standards: CNCA-C25-01:2024 (CCC implementation rules for EV charging equipment — effective 1 March 2025, supersedes any prior voluntary-only scheme; issued CNCA Announcement No. 25/2024)
Measures for the Administration of Compulsory Product Certification (SAMR 2020)
rows.gap: Chinese manufacturers exporting to Slovakia must create an EU-format DoC from scratch — listing each applicable EU directive, the specific harmonised standards applied, the manufacturer's name and address (or EU authorised representative's), and a traceable signatory. The CCC certificate neither replaces nor simplifies this. Test data generated for CCC may be re-used only if it was produced against equivalent EN test methods, which requires engineering review. ÚNMS SR as the Slovak market surveillance authority may request the DoC and technical file.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory — must accompany product or be available on request to ÚNMS SR or other market surveillance authorities
mandatory_status.cn: N/A — replaced by third-party CCC certificate regime

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] An EU DoC is a legal document that manufacturers or their EU representatives must sign and retain. It cannot be delegated to a test lab or certification body. Chinese exporters with only CCC documentation must draft the DoC in-house or engage an EU-based compliance consultant. ÚNMS SR is the Slovak market surveillance authority that may request this document.

rows.requirement: EU Economic Operator / Authorised Representative — Regulation (EU) 2019/1020
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and product compliance requires that products placed on the EU market have an identifiable 'responsible economic operator' established in the EU. For products manufactured outside the EU, this means the importer or, if no EU importer, a mandated EU authorised representative (Art. 4). The responsible operator must: hold the DoC and technical file or ensure they are accessible; register in RAPEX/ICSMS where required; cooperate with market surveillance authorities including ÚNMS SR in Slovakia; and take corrective action if a product is non-compliant.
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent requiring a domestic responsible operator for export-bound products. Chinese manufacturers exporting abroad appoint foreign distributors or agents commercially, but there is no statutory requirement to designate an EU-resident legal representative responsible for CE compliance and market surveillance cooperation.
rows.gap: This is a structural gap with no Chinese regulatory analogue. A Chinese EV charger manufacturer shipping directly to Slovak customers (e.g., via e-commerce) must appoint an EU-established authorised representative before the first unit enters the EU market. Without one, the product cannot legally be placed on the Slovak/EU market under Regulation 2019/1020. The AR must be named on the product label or documentation and must cooperate with ÚNMS SR on request.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for non-EU manufacturers without an EU importer

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Chinese manufacturers without an EU importer must appoint an EU-established authorised representative. This is a hard legal gate under Regulation 2019/1020 — no EU AR means the product cannot lawfully enter the Slovak/EU market, regardless of CE marking status. ÚNMS SR is the Slovak market surveillance authority.

rows.requirement: AFIR — Public EV Charging: Ad-hoc Payment, Interoperability and Technical Specifications
rows.target_requirement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR) mandates functional requirements for publicly accessible EV recharging points in Slovakia. AFIR-confirmed requirements include: (1) ad-hoc charging without a subscription or contract, with the payment instruments required by AFIR for relevant publicly accessible recharging points; (2) transparent price information before a charging session starts; (3) digital connectivity, smart recharging capability, static data and dynamic data obligations for publicly accessible infrastructure; (4) AFIR Annex II technical specifications for publicly accessible recharging points, including Type 2 for normal-power AC recharging points and Combo 2 for high-power DC recharging points; and (5) TEN-T deployment targets. AFIR replaces Directive 2014/94/EU (AFID) and is directly applicable in Slovakia.
target_standards: AFIR Annex II (technical specifications for publicly accessible recharging points)
rows.china_equivalent: China has no direct regulatory equivalent to AFIR's functional public-charging requirements. The closest standards are GB/T 34658 (interoperability requirements) and NB/T 33025 (communication protocols for EV charging), plus GB/T 27930 (DC charging communication). Chinese public chargers are increasingly connected via operator platforms, but AFIR-equivalent ad-hoc payment, data-access, smart recharging and EU connector requirements are not mandated by Chinese regulation.
china_standards: NB/T 33025-2016 (EV DC charging communication protocol — EVSE side)
GB/T 27930-2015 (communication protocol between off-board charger and BMS)
rows.gap: Significant functional gap for public charging deployments in Slovakia: (1) ad-hoc payment functionality may need to be added for EU public deployments; (2) digital connectivity, smart recharging, data-access and roaming/data exchange obligations may differ from proprietary Chinese operator platforms; (3) AFIR Annex II connector specifications (Type 2 / CCS2) differ from Chinese GB/T connector practice; (4) Slovak-language interface and documentation may be expected for end-user compliance and public tender requirements.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for publicly accessible recharging points in Slovakia under Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 (AFIR), directly applicable from 13 April 2024.
mandatory_status.cn: Not mandated — AFIR-equivalent ad-hoc payment, data-access, smart recharging and EU connector requirements are absent from Chinese public charging regulations.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] AFIR introduces functional requirements for publicly accessible charging points in Slovakia, including ad-hoc payment, price transparency, digital connectivity, smart recharging, data obligations and Annex II connector specifications. Chinese charger hardware intended for Slovak public deployment must be verified for AFIR compliance before installation. Slovak-language user interface and documentation may be required for public tenders and end-user acceptance.

rows.requirement: OCPP, EMC, Radio Modules, and Power Quality
rows.target_requirement: Networked EV chargers in Slovakia should be specified for OCPP back-office interoperability where a charge-point operator, fleet operator, public-sector project, or DSO-linked programme requires remote monitoring, billing, diagnostics, or load management. Electrical and electronic emissions and immunity evidence should align with IEC 61000 EMC and power-quality standards. Cellular, Wi-Fi, RFID, payment, or smart-metering modules may trigger additional communications, spectrum, cybersecurity, and data-interface checks under Slovak or EU requirements. Slovakia uses Central European frequency spectrum allocations; radio module type approvals granted only for China domestic use are not valid for Slovak deployment.
target_standards: OCPP — Open Charge Point Protocol for networked EV chargers
IEC 61000 series — electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
IEC 61851-24 — digital communication between DC EV charging station and EV
Directive 2014/53/EU (RED) — radio equipment requirements for wireless modules
Slovak telecommunications spectrum authority requirements for radio modules where in scope
rows.china_equivalent: China DC fast chargers commonly use GB/T 27930-2023 CAN communication between the off-board charger and vehicle BMS. This is not OCPP back-office communication and is not the CCS2 communication direction. China-market chargers may also include China-specific payment, SIM, cloud, and operator integrations that need reconfiguration for Slovak operators, roaming, language (Slovak), currency (Euro), and data interfaces.
china_standards: China radio module approvals where applicable
rows.gap: Exporters must confirm the OCPP version, charge-point-management-system integration, remote diagnostics, load management, payment or RFID flow, SIM or communications module approval path (RED and Slovak spectrum), and IEC 61000 EMC reports for the final Slovakia configuration. For DC CCS2 products, GB/T 27930 must not be presented as the relevant communication evidence. Harmonic current and immunity data should be reviewed against the specific Slovak DSO supply point constraints. Charger user interfaces and documentation are commonly expected in Slovak for public tender qualification and end-user acceptance.

mandatory_status.target: Project-specific but commonly mandatory for networked public, fleet, or utility-linked chargers in Slovakia; EMC and power-quality evidence is expected where required by ÚNMS, ÚRSO, DSO, tender, or site-owner specifications; RED compliance is mandatory for wireless-enabled chargers
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is China domestic DC vehicle-charger communication and is not OCPP or CCS2 back-office evidence

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Slovak networked chargers should be validated for OCPP integration, IEC 61000 EMC and power quality, RED compliance for wireless modules, and local communications-module requirements. GB/T 27930 alone does not satisfy OCPP, CCS2 communication, or back-office interoperability needs. Slovak-language user interface and documentation are commonly expected for public deployments.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)

rows.requirement: Low Voltage Safety — EV Charging Equipment (General)
rows.target_requirement: EV charging equipment placed on the Slovak/EU market must comply with the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU, ensuring it is designed and manufactured to be safe when correctly installed and maintained. Equipment must meet the Essential Safety Requirements (Annex I) covering protection against electric shock, insulation, overcurrent/overtemperature protection, and clearances. Harmonised standard EN IEC 61851-1:2019 (Mode 1–4 conductive charging, AC and DC, general requirements) provides a presumption of conformity. ÚNMS SR is the Slovak market surveillance authority responsible for LVD compliance oversight.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-1:2019 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 1: General requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly references GB/T 18487.1-2015 (Electric vehicle conductive charging system — General requirements), which is technically aligned with IEC 61851-1 but incorporates national deviations. It is enforced under the GB framework administered by SAMR/SAC. GB/T 18487.1 testing and certification by a Chinese CNAS-accredited lab is NOT recognised as equivalent to EN IEC 61851-1 testing under the EU LVD conformity assessment pathway in Slovakia.
china_standards: GB/T 18487.1-2015 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — General requirements (SAMR/SAC)
rows.gap: Exporters should build an EU conformity file against the LVD essential safety requirements and may use EN IEC 61851-1:2019 testing as evidence for presumption of conformity. Existing Chinese GB/T 18487.1 test reports do not automatically substitute because scope, deviations, connector assumptions and documentation differ. A Notified Body is not mandatory for LVD; manufacturer self-declaration with a Technical File is the normal route. Documentation gap: EU Declaration of Conformity, CE marking, and Slovak or EU-language technical instructions are all required. ÚNMS SR may conduct market surveillance inspections.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: Directive 2014/35/EU and CE marking before Slovak/EU market placement. EN IEC 61851-1:2019 is voluntary harmonised-standard evidence for presumption of conformity; alternative technical solutions are allowed if the manufacturer demonstrates compliance with the LVD essential safety requirements.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for domestic market — GB/T 18487.1 compliance required under SAMR framework

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] CE marking under LVD 2014/35/EU is mandatory for the Slovak market. EN IEC 61851-1:2019 is a voluntary harmonised standard that can grant presumption of conformity for general EV conductive charging; it is not the legal obligation itself. Chinese GB/T 18487.1 certification does not by itself satisfy the EU conformity assessment pathway; EU evidence against the LVD requirements is needed. ÚNMS SR is the Slovak market surveillance authority.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)

rows.requirement: DC Charging Station Safety — EV Conductive Charging
rows.target_requirement: DC charging stations (Mode 4, off-board chargers) placed on the Slovak/EU market must comply with the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU where within scope. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 (Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 23: DC EV charging station) is a current product standard that may be used as technical evidence and, where cited as harmonised, gives presumption of conformity; it is not itself the mandatory legal obligation. Key technical topics include isolation monitoring, interlock systems, control pilot functions, maximum voltage/current ratings, and communication protocols for DC supply. For Slovakia, this must include CCS2 connector compatibility and ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 communication stack alignment.
target_standards: EN IEC 61851-23:2023 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 23: DC EV charging station (current edition, supersedes 2014)
rows.china_equivalent: China's DC charging station domestic equivalent is GB/T 18487.5-2024 (DC charging system for GB/T 20234.3 connector) and GB/T 20234.3-2023 (DC charging coupler, supports up to 1500 V / 800 A). CQC or CNAS certification to these Chinese standards is not accepted under the EU LVD CE marking pathway in Slovakia.
china_standards: GB/T 18487.5-2024 — Electric vehicle conductive charging system — Part 5: DC charging system for GB/T 20234.3 (current DC system standard)
GB/T 20234.3-2023 — Connection set for conductive charging of electric vehicles — Part 3: DC charging coupler (supersedes 2015 edition)
rows.gap: DC charging stations exported to Slovakia should be assessed against the LVD essential safety requirements. Particular attention is needed for: (1) CCS2 (Combined Charging System Type 2) connector compliance vs. Chinese GB/T connector — a hardware redesign is required; (2) ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 communication protocol compatibility for Slovak/EU CCS2 deployments, vs. GB/T 27930 CAN which is not compatible; (3) isolation monitoring requirements per European grid topology (TN-S or TT earthing systems commonly used in Slovakia). The connector type itself is a hard hardware gap.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation: CE marking under Directive 2014/35/EU where the charger is within LVD scope. EN IEC 61851-23:2023 is a voluntary technical standard that may support presumption of conformity where harmonised/cited; alternatives are allowed if the manufacturer demonstrates compliance with the Directive.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory — GB/T 18487.5-2024 is the current DC charging system standard; CCC mandatory from 1 March 2025 under CNCA-C25-01:2024

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] DC charging stations require CE marking under the applicable EU legislation for the Slovak market, including LVD where in scope. Chinese GB/T 18487.5 certification is not accepted as an EU conformity assessment substitute. A significant hardware gap exists where Chinese DC stations use GB/T connectors incompatible with EU CCS2 practice; the communication protocol (GB/T 27930 CAN) is also incompatible with Slovak/EU ISO 15118 / DIN 70121 CCS2 deployments.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)

rows.requirement: Electrical Installation Safety — EV Charging in Buildings (IEC 60364-7-722)
rows.target_requirement: Slovak electrical installation law and grid/installer rules govern the building-side circuits supplying EV charging points. IEC 60364-7-722 / HD 60364-7-722 provide the commonly adopted technical installation route covering protective measures (RCD type B or A+DC detection), wiring, earthing, and load management. Slovakia has adopted HD 60364-7-722 as the national standard (STN HD 60364-7-722). These standards apply to the building-side installation infrastructure, not the charger product itself, but exported EV chargers should be compatible with these installation requirements so they can be accepted by Slovak installers and DSOs.
target_standards: IEC 60364-7-722:2018 — Low-voltage electrical installations — Part 7-722: Requirements for special installations or locations — Supply of electric vehicles
HD 60364-7-722 (CENELEC harmonised document, adopted in Slovakia as STN HD 60364-7-722)
rows.china_equivalent: China addresses EV charging installation primarily through GB 50966-2014 (Code for design of electric vehicle charging station) and GB/T 51313-2018 (Technical standard for electric vehicle charging infrastructure), administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD). These cover site design and installation but differ from IEC 60364-7-722 in RCD type requirements, earthing system assumptions (TN-S vs. Chinese practice), and load management protocols. Chinese installation documentation is not accepted as evidence of compliance with Slovak/EU member-state installation standards.
china_standards: GB 50966-2014 — Code for design of electric vehicle charging station (MOHURD) (confirmed to exist; enforced by MOHURD/MIIT)
GB/T 51313-2018 — Technical standard for electric vehicle charging infrastructure (confirmed to exist; enforced by MOHURD/MIIT)
rows.gap: STN HD 60364-7-722 governs building-side EV installation practice in Slovakia. EV chargers exported to Slovakia should declare compatibility with Type B RCDs or incorporate internal DC fault protection to allow Type A RCDs under Slovak installation practice. A charger that requires installation conditions not achievable under Slovak electrical codes will fail field acceptance by Slovak DSOs and building inspectors. Chinese charger datasheets often omit compatibility statements expected by Slovak installers. Installation documentation and instructions must be provided in Slovak.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory legal obligation sits in Slovak electrical installation law, DSO rules, and building permitting/inspection requirements. STN HD 60364-7-722 is the commonly adopted technical standard for EV charging installation in Slovakia; product compatibility is a practical market requirement. Installation instructions in Slovak are required.
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for domestic installation — GB 50966 / GB/T 51313 under MOHURD (confirmed as published standards enforced by MOHURD; check SAC for any 2023-2025 revisions)

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] STN HD 60364-7-722 governs building-side EV charging installation practice in Slovakia. EV chargers exported to Slovakia should be compatible with the RCD and earthing requirements expected by Slovak installers and DSOs. This is distinct from product-level CE marking under LVD, but non-compatibility can block field installation. Chinese installation standards (GB 50966 / GB/T 51313) are not substitutes. Installation instructions must be in Slovak.

source.publisher: Slovak Office of Standards, Metrology and Testing (ÚNMS SR)
